To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effects of high school characteristics on future earnings are not uniform across all schools; (2) the effects of school characteristics on future earning are not uniform across the entire student population, but vary by race and sex; (3) the effects of schools are not uniform across students who are similar in their individual background characteristics, but vary by individual characteristics; and (4) the effects of the high school environment on future earnings are enduring.
(1) the effects of school on future earnings are substantial and positive, and (2) there are significant differences in the magnitude of these effects across school types.
